_comment: Doc map — foundation doc §6.5. Maps code areas to manual sections.
It sits at the repo root rather than under docs/ because it is the contract
*between* the two halves of the monorepo, and belongs to neither. Both `code`
and `pages` are therefore repo-root-relative; see README.md.
JSON rather than YAML only because the prototype matches it with jq inside
the Jenkins container. The real docbot CLI reads YAML (§6.5); keep that
shape when porting. `code` entries are regexes matched against changed
file paths as GitLab reports them.
Explicit no-doc-impact entries matter as much as positive ones: they record
why the gate stays silent so nobody rediscovers it later.
The monorepo entry. With docs and code in one repository, DocBot's own
output merges into the same main branch that triggers DocBot — so the
manual is an input to the gate unless something says otherwise. This
entry says otherwise: docs/ is the destination, never the trigger.
It is a second line of defence, not the first. docbot already skips
merge requests carrying the `docbot-generated` label, which stops the
loop at the source. This entry additionally covers the case that label
cannot: a human editing the manual by hand.
